items.title: Keep PyInstaller CArchive members inside the payload
items.deduplication: Outer CArchive payload ranges; earlier #398 concerns encryption-key hints and #707 inner PYZ ranges.
items.body:
## Problem
CArchive member offsets were checked against the whole executable when reading. A malformed table could therefore expose the archive table, cookie or bytes appended by signing as member contents, and an out-of-range PYZ could supply a fabricated nested listing.

## Change
Require each stored member range to end before the CArchive table. Keep the outer listing and valid members, mark invalid ranges unreadable, and explain the limitation. Empty runtime options at the payload boundary remain valid.

## Validation
Added regressions for both cookie formats, crossing the payload boundary, table/cookie/signed-tail offsets, empty options and a valid PYZ placed in the signed tail.

Exact source commit `a5bcfaedcb1ad67c8bb7f06c7143befc8292409c` passed formatting, all 952 formats tests, and all-targets clippy with warnings denied in [remote validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226891917). The workflow runs in Afloat16/claude-mem and checks out this exact craft-anything revision.

With production code fixed at upstream `1b5f516b07277036e9e6cca5e75c0a5ebdfcd9f1`, the [test-only baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226895582) fails `members_cannot_read_the_table_cookie_or_signed_tail` and `a_pyz_in_the_signed_tail_does_not_supply_nested_members`. The same regression cases pass in this branch.

Layers, locks, secret scanning, WebAssembly checks and an unchanged Cargo.lock also passed for this exact revision in [the supplementary verification](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42640688213/job/129240669663).

[Exact-head verification](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42649592140) is in progress; the successful checks above refer to the earlier verified source.

items.title: Reject ASAR manifest nodes with invalid file metadata
items.deduplication: Manifest node grammar and required file metadata; earlier #702 is header framing, #1142 rejected-name budgets and #533 output names.
items.body:
## Problem
ASAR JSON nodes with the wrong shape or missing file metadata were silently treated as empty files, and a non-object files map was accepted as an empty archive. That produces a plausible but incorrect inventory of damaged manifests.

## Change
Validate directory maps, node objects, link values, unsigned file sizes, packed offsets and unpacked markers. Keep valid empty files, numeric offsets, links and unpacked files supported, while retaining existing name and listing limits.

## Validation
Added malformed-manifest fixtures and valid controls.

items.title: Validate gzip header checksums without rejecting informational fields
items.deduplication: Gzip FHCRC and informational header fields; no substantive matching PR in the reviewed full-body history.
items.body:
## Problem
Gzip headers with an FHCRC were accepted even when the header checksum was wrong, while otherwise readable streams were rejected solely for informational XFL or OS values.

## Change
Check the low 16 bits of the header CRC-32 when FHCRC is present. Accept informational encoder bytes and preserve checks for the compression method, reserved flag bits, optional-field boundaries and trailer integrity.

The framing follows [RFC 1952 section 2.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1952#section-2.3.1).

## Validation
Added complete optional-header fixtures, header-bit corruption, truncated FHCRC, informational-byte coverage and reserved-bit controls.

Exact source commit `dde4aa0233be968f9b55bd3316204b880b8dbf2e` passed formatting, all 952 formats tests, and all-targets clippy with warnings denied in [remote validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226891865). items.title: Read complete gzip packed members and verify their trailers
items.deduplication: Packed gzip trailer integrity and complete member consumption; separate from earlier manifest decoded-size checks.
items.body:
## Problem
The packed-file reader stripped a gzip header and inflated only the first DEFLATE stream. It could return damaged contents without checking CRC/ISIZE, accept missing trailers, and silently drop later gzip members.

## Change
Use the shared gzip reader to validate each member and consume the entire stored range. Concatenated members share the caller's output budget; size-limit failures retain the TooLarge error, while damaged or trailing bytes produce an error. Manifest-size checks remain in place.

## Validation
Added trailer corruption/truncation, trailing garbage, concatenation, empty-stream and aggregate-limit regressions. Updated the optional-header fixture to carry a real header checksum and trailer.

Exact source commit `3f3ec6a4bd97bb987d9cad906ce4b2f5028ff88b` passed formatting, all 952 formats tests, and all-targets clippy with warnings denied in [remote validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226891924). items.title: Extract ZIP entries compressed with bzip2 or XZ
items.deduplication: ZIP methods 12 and 95 extraction using already present codecs; no substantive matching PR in the reviewed full-body history.
items.body:
## Problem
The ZIP directory recognized bzip2 (12) and XZ (95), but extraction rejected both even though the formats crate already includes pure-Rust decoders for these streams.

## Change
Route both ZIP methods through the existing decompressors, preserving TooLarge errors, decoded-size validation and CRC checks. This adds no dependency and keeps encrypted entries unsupported.

## Validation
Added complete ZIP fixtures using the existing reference-encoder streams, plus corrupted data, understated directory sizes, exact/insufficient limits, CRC mismatch and encrypted controls.

items.title: Extract ZIP LZMA members with checked framing and output limits
items.deduplication: ZIP method 14 property/framing support; no substantive matching PR in the reviewed full-body history.
items.body:
## Problem
ZIP entries using LZMA method 14 are listed but cannot be read. Their property header and optional end-marker framing differ from standalone .lzma files, so passing the bytes to the existing standalone decoder would not work.

## Change
Read the ZIP-specific property header, select the decoder's size/end-marker mode from general-purpose bit 1, and bound the decoder dictionary and output. Require complete consumption and retain the existing decoded-size and CRC checks. No dependency is added.

Format reference: [PKWARE APPNOTE section 5.8](https://pkware.cachefly.net/webdocs/casestudies/APPNOTE.TXT).

## Validation
Added generated full ZIP fixtures for both framing modes, zero literals, limits, mismatched size/CRC, damaged properties, oversized dictionaries, truncated and trailing streams.

items.title: Enforce standalone LZMA budgets before large dictionary growth
items.deduplication: Public standalone decompress::lzma had no dictionary budget. Earlier #888 only protects the Unity-specific lzma_raw_complete path.
items.body:
## Problem
The standalone .lzma reader used default decoder options. Its capped output sink was reached only after the decoder flushed an internal dictionary, so small output budgets could still require large dictionary growth or processing of a damaged tail first.

## Change
Read the standalone size header before decoding, reject declared output above the budget, and bound the decoder's internal dictionary as well as the output sink. Preserve the decoder's 4 KiB minimum window and accept oversized dictionary properties for small valid streams.

This fixes the public standalone reader; the existing Unity raw-piece helper already has its own bounds and is unchanged.

## Validation
Added public-reader regressions for declared sizes, dictionary properties, exact/zero budgets and an over-budget stream with a damaged tail.

Exact source commit `5da8880d3b56785498cf0c09ae46f300f070322d` passed formatting, all 952 formats tests, and all-targets clippy with warnings denied in [remote validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226892150). items.title: Preserve GNU tar member identities at the long-name limit
items.deduplication: GNU LongName/LongLink identity truncation; earlier #1135 is numeric fields, #1136 PAX record framing and #1246 PAX extent/name recovery.
items.body:
## Problem
GNU LongName and LongLink metadata was cut to 4096 bytes before conversion to text. A longer member name or link target therefore appeared under a different, truncated identity, which could collide with a real shorter member.

## Change
Inspect the declared metadata without copying past the name budget. Accept complete identities at the limit, including size-delimited names and early NUL termination. Stop with a warning on an oversized identity or incomplete extension body, preserving earlier members.

## Validation
Added long-name and long-link fixtures beyond and exactly at the limit, earlier-member recovery, and short terminated names in padded extension data.

items.title: Keep GNU sparse tar payloads out of regular-file extraction
items.deduplication: GNU sparse PAX interpretation and extraction classification; existing old-GNU type S and PAX framing fixes do not cover it.
items.body:
## Problem
GNU PAX sparse archives store extents (and, in version 1.0, a sparse map) instead of the full logical file. The tar walker ignored the sparse metadata and listed these bytes as an ordinary file, allowing extraction of incorrect contents.

## Change
Recognize GNU.sparse metadata, retain GNU.sparse.name when present, and mark the member unsupported with an explicit reconstruction warning. Carry this state across extension headers and clear it after the member, so following ordinary files remain readable.

## Validation
Added original synthetic sparse 0.0/0.1/1.0 fixtures, member alignment and following-file controls, plus intervening GNU/PAX extensions.

Exact source commit `daaeb4fe6c2db3f805fb9b02f9fbdfe55d80eb4a` passed formatting, all 952 formats tests, and all-targets clippy with warnings denied in [remote validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226895529). items.title: Decode concatenated XZ streams and standard stream padding
items.deduplication: Standalone XZ concatenation and stream padding; no substantive matching PR in the reviewed full-body history.
items.body:
## Problem
The existing XZ decoder expects EOF immediately after one footer. It rejects valid standalone .xz files containing concatenated streams or the standard four-byte stream padding.

## Change
Find stream boundaries backwards using checksummed footers and indexes, then decode each bounded stream in order through one capped sink. Validate index integer encodings, aggregate declared output and padding alignment. No search for magic bytes inside compressed payloads is needed.

Format reference: [XZ file format sections 2 and 4](https://tukaani.org/xz/xz-file-format.txt).

## Validation
Added reference/generated fixtures for multiple and empty streams, padding, exact/insufficient aggregate budgets, truncated later members, damaged checksums and malformed index fields. This retains the existing backing decoder; it does not add a separate hard bound to that decoder's internal XZ block allocation.

Exact source commit `cd5d8c7006070db9b220d9397346de9cecd89900` passed formatting, all 953 formats tests, and all-targets clippy with warnings denied in [remote validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226895411). The workflow runs in Afloat16/claude-mem and checks out this exact craft-anything revision.

With production code fixed at upstream `1b5f516b07277036e9e6cca5e75c0a5ebdfcd9f1`, the [test-only baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42636776430/job/129226895582) fails `xz_concatenated_streams_and_padding_share_one_budget`. The same regression cases pass in this branch.

post_merge_followups.title: Refuse incomplete tar engine installs after GNU metadata stops

baseline.summary: test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 4 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 119 filtered out; finished in 0.01s

post_merge_followups.body:
## Problem

A tar listing can retain earlier members after a GNU long-name or long-link record is refused. The managed engine installer previously treated that partial inventory as a successful extraction whenever an earlier regular file existed. That can replace an engine installation with incomplete contents.

This is a follow-up to #1362, prepared from upstream `efddbdeb6868f10a3d8d53f114d47aed72b89612` after that PR merged.

## Change

- Record an explicit typed stop reason for oversized or truncated GNU name metadata, while retaining earlier members for inspection.
- Check that reason in the installer before writing any member. Oversized metadata returns `OverLimit`; truncated metadata returns `GarbledOutput`.
- Keep the existing compatibility for readable tar members without an end-of-archive marker. CPIO behavior and successful bounded GNU names remain unchanged.

## Regression evidence

The test-only revision `24d844ce89c6ea660e41f30be676411b25b06490` keeps production code at upstream `efddbdeb6868f10a3d8d53f114d47aed72b89612`. Its [actual baseline run](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42648642576/job/129268658248) reports **4 failed and 2 passed**: oversized/truncated long names and long links each write an earlier file on the old code; missing end markers and valid bounded metadata are passing controls.

The fixed tests also assert that an existing installed file is unchanged when extraction is refused. Formats tests check that partial listing bytes remain readable and that absent end markers do not receive the new stop reason.

## Verification

Exact source revision: `3e588c5589ee56ab50004dd0e87cc47f4f2455da`.
The [exact-source validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42649935938/job/129273248608) passed formatting, all **1,141 tests** (**124 engines + 1,017 formats**), all-targets clippy with warnings denied, layers, locks, secret scanning, WebAssembly checks and Cargo.lock stability. One existing network-download test remains ignored. The workflow checks out this craft-anything revision in Afloat16/claude-mem.

Branch head `1007aae934ea3d17fbe341daa7851a1c79eda7a6` adds only the completed roadmap entry, status evidence and the parser/installer lesson in `docs/pitfalls.md`; source and test files are unchanged from the tested revision.

Roadmap: R3.12.
